images.caption: Figure 1:Three execution paradigms.Top left, single-round:the router selects one Worker for a single call.Top right, multi-round:the router selects Workers sequentially using accumulated observations.Bottom, agentic:the router selects Workers, assigns roles, and specifies dependencies between calls; the depicted workflow is illustrative, and its roles and dependencies vary across queries.

Figure 2:Overview ofRouteWeaver.(a)One routing policyπθ\pi_{\theta}selects an execution mode, then calls frozen Workers;Multi-round calls automatically use the latest observation, while agentic calls include role assignments and router-selected references to earlier outputs.Returned observations are appended to its context until it emits the final answer.(b)COMET-GRPO computes mode-level and within-mode advantages per reward component, mixes them (Eq. (7)), and assignsAimodeA_{i}^{\mathrm{mode}}to mode-selection tokens andAiinnerA_{i}^{\mathrm{inner}}to subsequent router tokens.(c)Progressive training moves mode selection from assigned modes to the router in three stages.
